name: Archival / Historical
summary: Documents, maps and press clippings on aged paper with grain and foxing, documentary serif type and slow dissolves. Motion is a camera moving over a surface.

identity.visual_language: documents, maps, newsprint and halftone photographs
identity.editorial_approach: evidence on screen, attributable and legible
identity.composition_philosophy: a surface seen by a slow camera
identity.storytelling_conventions: zoom into a detail, pull back to the whole page, dissolve in time

typography.mono: IBM Plex Mono for typewriter and dates

composition.principles: documents layered at slight angles; text legible when it is evidence

design_system.lighting: even raking light on a surface

motion.grammar: A slow camera over documents; dissolves for time passing; nothing bounces.

camera.language: slow push, lateral track over a document

motion.stillness_policy: Held documents keep slow drift and grain.

rendering.strategy: HyperFrames layered documents with procedural paper and grain; period imagery must be licensed or generated and labelled as such.
rendering.resource_notes: Authentic archival media needs sourcing and rights checks.

provenance.method: Authored rule set (prescribed). Derived from the style system's tokens, the workspace motion vocabulary and the technique records listed; not extracted from a single reference.
provenance.notes: Every value here is prescribed intent, not a measurement. Evidence of use is recorded under 'validation' only after a render exists.

weaknesses: Generated 'archival' imagery risks passing as authentic: label it.
Period typography without period facts can mislead.
example_scenes: A map pinned on a table; the camera pushes to a marked street while a typed caption appears.
